stories.title: Deterministic in-process reproducer for the DriveDetector close-signal defect (RED)
stories.completionNotes: Reproducer shipped: tests/pi/obdii/drive/test_drive2829_close_signal_reproducer.py. Reuses the proven US-359 InjectedClock harness (patches datetime in detector+types modules -> deterministic, no wall-clock, no time.sleep). RPM-ONLY sequences, NO comms events (no BATTERY_V heartbeat) -- a 'missed close' is modelled by the ABSENCE of ticks (readings stop @ 20s, before the 60s RPM-debounce completes; no heartbeat to drive the US-229 ECU-silence path either), exactly the US-386 contract. 4 tests: (a) clean short ~3min drive = GREEN control (1 closed id, proves harness yields correct attribution); (b) back-to-back ~1min apart w/ missed first close + (c) key-on a full day after a missed close = RED-as-xfail, each asserts CORRECT behavior (2 distinct closed drive_ids, no absorption); + determinism (two runs identical). VC#1: normal run = 2 passed + 2 xfailed (suite GREEN); --runxfail confirms both stale-open tests fail RED with got=[1] -- one drive_id absorbing TWO physical drives (the missed-close/stale-open-leak half of the 28/29 signature). VC#2 (back-to-back) confirmed: second drive absorbed into id #1, ids NOT minted per-physical-drive. SCOPE/RCA-BOUNDARY (does NOT trip the conditionalOutcome -- the substantive Root-2 defect DOES reproduce in-process): the connection_log *overlap* (two ids open at once, out of temporal order) is Root 1 = concurrent-process (two eclipse-obd PIDs racing the shared drive_counter, per Atlas's 2026-06-19 RCA), which a SINGLE in-process detector cannot produce by construction (the only exit from RUNNING is _endDrive, which writes the matching drive_end) -- it is mitigated out-of-band + made durable by US-389 and backstopped server-side by US-390. This in-process harness faithfully reproduces the Root-2 stale-open/missed-close/absorption half that US-388 must fix. Note filed to PM/Atlas inbox documenting the boundary. xfail markers are strict=False (US-359 precedent); US-388 removes them when its fix flips the two scenarios GREEN. mypy not installed on this dev box -> Typecheck AC deferred to PM/Atlas make typecheck at integration (code is mypy-strict-shaped: future annotations + full hints). stories.title: RCA: root-cause the DriveDetector close / drive-end path
stories.completionNotes: RCA shipped: docs/rca/2026-06-28-us387-drivedetector-close-signal-rca.md. No production code change (research story; AC 'no fix in this story'). LOAD-BEARING FINDING: the entire drive-close state machine is TICK-DRIVEN ONLY -- processValue (detector.py:521) is the sole evaluator of every close decision, and it is called from exactly one place in the running system: EventRouter._handleReading (event_router.py:404-407). No independent timer/watchdog thread. Therefore when readings stop, NO close decision is ever evaluated; and _handleConnectionLost (event_router.py:522-556) does NOT close a drive (never touches the detector). Root 2 (US-388, substantive): engine-off RPM=0 ticks stop @ ~20s < driveEndDurationSeconds 60s -> the STOPPING->drive_end debounce comparison (detector.py:665-672) is never re-evaluated; with NO adapter heartbeat (Spool ruled out comms-drop) the ECU-silence backstop (_checkEcuSilenceDriveEnd detector.py:932-986, called detector.py:569) never fires either. A later key-on then CONTINUES the stale RUNNING/STOPPING session (detector.py:655-677 clears belowThresholdSince, back to RUNNING) -- _startDrive/_openDriveId (detector.py:735/1208) never reached -> the 2nd physical drive is ABSORBED into the 1st's id, no new mint. US-361 _isEcuSilenceContinuation (detector.py:988-1019) does NOT cover this -- it requires a silence drive_end to have fired; here the close never happens. Root 1 (overlap / out-of-temporal-order ids, US-389/US-390): two concurrent eclipse-obd processes racing the shared drive_counter -- nextDriveId (drive_id.py:211-231) lacks the BEGIN IMMEDIATE its own docstring warns multi-connection callers to use; _currentDriveId is a PER-PROCESS module singleton (drive_id.py:265-266) so neither process sees the other's open drive. NOT in-process reproducible by construction (one _currentSession detector.py:218; only _endDrive detector.py:790 exits RUNNING). ONE-ROOT HYPOTHESIS REFUTED -> two INDEPENDENT roots: Root 2 = single-process state-machine bug producing ABSORPTION (fewer ids than drives); Root 1 = deploy/process-singleton bug producing OVERLAP (more, out-of-order ids). Distinct mechanisms, distinct fixes, distinct reproducibility. Spool's connection_log finding (drive_start=29/drive_end=18; zero drive_id on comms failure) incorporated (doc §5): 29/18 is dominated by Root-2 missed-closes; comms-drop ruled out -> models the missed close as the ABSENCE of ticks (exactly the US-386 RPM-only harness). VC#1 SATISFIED: reproducer --runxfail confirms both stale-open scenarios got=[1] (absorption) mapping exactly to the Root-2 trace; control + determinism GREEN (2 passed, 2 xfailed normal mode -- zero regression, no code touched). VC#2 (Atlas accepts root cause = gate for US-388) is an EXTERNAL gate routed to Atlas (offices/architect/inbox/2026-06-28-from-rex-us387-rca-ready-for-review.md) -- pending Atlas review, NOT in Ralph's hands; mirrors US-386's deferred-Atlas precedent. US-388 stays BUILD-BLOCKED (A-11) until that sign-off lands.

stories.title: dtc_freeze_frame sync: quarantine unresolvable cross-tier rows after N failures (stop silent infinite retry)
stories.completionNotes: Shipped queue-level quarantine, Pi-side (data_quality/status-flag approach -- Atlas quick-read blessed it as Ralph-pickable; NO new cross-tier table, so the conditionalOutcome's route-to-Atlas did NOT fire). DESIGN PIN: the story goal sentence is decisive -- 'fail loudly, no silent re-resolve is correct per-attempt but wrong at the queue level' -- so the SERVER resolution is UNCHANGED (_resolveVehicleInfoIdForCapture still raises -> 500 per attempt); the fix lives entirely in the Pi sync QUEUE (sync_log + SyncClient). Architectural facts that pinned Pi-side: (1) there is NO server-side per-table HWM -- last_synced_id lives only in the Pi sync_log, so AC5 is about the Pi cursor; (2) dtc_freeze_frame is pushed in its OWN per-table batch (pushAllDeltas -> pushDelta(tableName) -> single-table payload), so 'does not block other tables' is already structural -- the real harm was the ~27x/day failed-push NOISE masking real failures; (3) PRD cross-story note + AC4 ('throttled/retryable, NOT terminal') => quarantine == THROTTLE: after N consecutive failures stop retrying every cycle, auto-redrain when the throttle window elapses (or on forcePush), and never advance the HWM so the raw record is preserved + re-drainable (US-149 invariant). MECHANISM: sync_log gains consecutive_failures + quarantined_at (idempotent ensureQuarantineSchema ALTER; fresh DBs get them in SYNC_LOG_SCHEMA) + recordPushFailure/getQuarantineState/clearQuarantine. SyncClient: injected clock (deterministic throttle), PushStatus.QUARANTINED (skip with NO network call while throttled), surface-ONCE on the transition (single 'SYNC_QUARANTINE' WARNING), clearQuarantine on any successful push, forcePush bypasses the throttle (explicit deploy-time re-drain -- satisfies the PRD US-367<->US-391 're-drain after US-367 lands' gate), _PushFailure.serverRejected so ONLY server HTTP-rejections count toward quarantine (transient network DNS/refused/timeout do NOT -- a WiFi outage can't wrongly quarantine a healthy table). Config: pi.companionService.quarantineThreshold (5) + quarantineThrottleSeconds (3600) in validator DEFAULTS + config.json + _validateCompanionService range checks (bool-rejected-first). AC MAP: AC1 stop-after-N (recordPushFailure threshold) + AC2 preserve-raw (HWM never advances; raw row never dropped -- VC2 test asserts row still exists) + AC3 surface-once (transition-only WARNING -- test asserts exactly 1 across 3 fails + 1 throttled cycle) + AC4 re-drainable (throttle-elapse + forcePush; clearQuarantine on success) + AC5 no-HWM-advance + does-not-block-other-tables (per-table; quarantine is per-table) + AC6 test proves N-fail->quarantine->single-surface->re-drain (test_sync_client_quarantine.py::test_quarantineLifecycle_nFailsThenThrottleThenRedrain). GATES: ruff clean on all 7 touched files; tests/pi/sync/ + tests/pi/data/ + tests/test_config_validator.py = all green EXCEPT one PRE-EXISTING unrelated red (test_client_config_paths.py::test_validatorOutput_constructsSyncClient asserts the dead .10 server IP; default is .120 since the 2026-06-18 relocation -- US-391 never touches baseUrl; filed offices/pm/issues/I-stale-sync-client-baseurl-test-old-ip.md, candidate fold into US-392); python validate_config.py green. mypy NOT installed on this dev box -> Typecheck AC deferred to PM/Atlas `make typecheck` at integration (code is mypy-strict-shaped: future annotations + full hints). Full `pytest tests/` deferred to PM integration (slow SMB); scoped suites covering the change ran green in-iteration. stories.title: De-dup the server address inside config.json (derive base URLs from serverHost:serverPort)
stories.completionNotes: A-15 server-address de-dup shipped: config.json now holds the server IP in EXACTLY ONE key (server.network.serverHost) -- the serverBaseUrl and pi.companionService.baseUrl literals are removed and DERIVED. DESIGN: JSON can't self-reference and the secrets_loader only expands env-vars, so derivation lives in the validator (the load/defaults layer), mirroring deploy/addresses.sh's existing SERVER_BASE_URL=${SERVER_HOST}:${SERVER_PORT} pattern. New ConfigValidator._deriveServerUrls (runs after _applyDefaults) sets server.network.serverBaseUrl + pi.companionService.baseUrl to http://{serverHost}:{serverPort} ONLY WHEN ABSENT -- an explicit baseUrl still wins (addresses.sh ':-' fallback semantics), so the ~15 test fixtures that pass baseUrl directly + every runtime consumer (SyncClient, update_checker, HomeNetworkDetector) resolve the IDENTICAL value as before (AC2 no behavioral change). DEFAULTS: dropped the 'pi.companionService.baseUrl' literal; added 'server.network.serverHost'(=10.27.27.120, b044-exempt mirror) + 'server.network.serverPort'(=8000) as the validator-side single source + the fallback when a config omits the server.network section. AC3: scripts/audit_address_mirrors.py + tests/lint/test_address_mirror_consistency.py REWORKED to the single-source model (named in the AC) -- the parsers + compareMirrors now cross-check the host/port/hostname fact across config.json <> addresses.sh <> validator DEFAULTS (the real 2026-06-18 drift guard, KEPT + extended to validator serverHost/serverPort); the obsolete intra-config base-URL literal checks are retired because there is no longer a base-URL literal to drift. conditionalOutcome did NOT fire: hasRouteToServer (the offline IP-route probe) parses its host FROM self.baseUrl, which is now the DERIVED URL still carrying the IP -- it needs no separate key, so no special-case IP resolution was added; and the A-15 hostname-resolution DESIGN change (separate story) was NOT folded in (IPs stay IPs). Also closed the pre-existing red I-stale-sync-client-baseurl-test-old-ip: test_validatorOutput_constructsSyncClient now derives its expectation from the validated config's serverHost:serverPort (drift-proof) instead of the dead .10 literal -- the .10 default is gone entirely. stories.title: Fix stale harness fixture after US-371 drive_id->summary_id rename (test-only)
stories.completionNotes: Test-only fixture fix shipped (no src/ change -- product ORM already correct since US-371). ROOT CAUSE: the synthetic divergence fixture in test_harnessTooling_canCatchSchemaVsOrmDivergence_synthetic built its historical drive_statistics table with the PRE-US-371 `drive_id` column, so the Phase-1 production-ORM INSERT (which references summary_id + data_quality) raised OperationalError on 'no such column: summary_id' FIRST -- a rename artifact -- NOT the intended I-041 'no such column: data_quality' symptom; the assertion `"data_quality" in errMsg` therefore tripped RED for the wrong reason. CONFIRMED RED-FOR-WRONG-REASON before fix: run yielded 'table drive_statistics has no column named summary_id'. FIX (single edit, 3 SQL identifiers + 1 comment): historical CREATE TABLE block now declares `summary_id INTEGER NOT NULL`, `PRIMARY KEY (summary_id, parameter_name)`, `FOREIGN KEY (summary_id) REFERENCES drive_summary(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` -- matching the ORM (models.py:1046 summary_id Mapped, the US-371 rename is complete/no alias). Now the ONLY divergence from the ORM is the missing data_quality column, so Phase 1 raises OperationalError mentioning data_quality (AC3 right-reason) and Phase 2 (ALTER ADD COLUMN data_quality) INSERT succeeds. conditionalOutcome did NOT fire -- kept the default single-symptom (data_quality) intent; no Atlas/Argus split ruling needed (the fixture's sole purpose is the data_quality seam, and DriveStatistic has exactly two divergences from the historical shape: the drive_id->summary_id rename + the v0009 data_quality add, so fixing the rename leaves data_quality as the clean single symptom). The other `drive_id` references in the file are the legitimate DriveSummary.drive_id column (a DIFFERENT table -- the Pi-assigned drive id) + its seeding, untouched. GATES: VC1 target test PASSED (right reason -- the data_quality assertion held); VC2 `pytest tests/integration -m "not slow"` = 18 passed (zero regression, no summary_id-missing failures introduced); VC3 grep confirms the historical block declares summary_id not drive_id (lines 784/794/795); ruff clean on the touched file. mypy NOT installed on this dev box -> Typecheck deferred to PM/Atlas `make typecheck` at integration (test-only change, no type surface added). Committed 7193b0b.
